dublinCore.dc:title: 119 HR 9887 IH: Swatting Registry Best Practices Act
dublinCore.dc:rights: Pursuant to Title 17 Section 105 of the United States Code, this file is not subject to copyright protection and is in the public domain.

action.action-desc: Mr. Walkinshaw (for himself and Ms. Lee of Florida) introduced the following bill; which was referred to the Committee on the Judiciary

form.official-title: To establish a registry to reduce swatting, and for other purposes.

section.text: This Act may be cited as the Swatting Registry Best Practices Act.

section.header: Development and issuance of guidance on swatting registries

subsection.text: Not later than 1 year after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Attorney General, in consultation with the Secretary of Homeland Security, shall develop and issue guidance, which shall include best practices for State, Tribal, territorial, and local governments and public safety agencies regarding the establishment, operation, and oversight of voluntary swatting registries and related public safety protocols.
In developing the guidance under subsection (a), the Attorney General shall consult with—

paragraph.text: State, local, Tribal, and territorial law enforcement agencies and public safety answering points, including those serving large, mid-sized, and rural jurisdictions;
public safety, emergency communications, and 9–1–1 system experts with experience in call-taking, dispatch, computer-aided dispatch systems, and incident response protocols;

privacy, cybersecurity, data governance, and civil liberties experts with demonstrated technical expertise in the secure design, operation, oversight, and auditing of sensitive public safety databases;

disability access, language access, and victim services experts with demonstrated expertise in ensuring voluntary registry programs are accessible to individuals who may face elevated risks of swatting or targeting harassment;
technology providers and 9–1–1 system vendors with relevant expertise in secure database design, caller authentication, and call-handling protocols; and
individuals and households who have been victims of swatting incidents.
The guidance required under subsection (a) shall include, at a minimum, the following:

subparagraph.text: The best practices for designing voluntary swatting registries that—

clause.text: allow voluntary opt-in by residents;
identify categories of higher-risk registrants, including individuals reasonably believed to face an elevated risk of swatting or targeting harassment;
provide clear criteria and procedures for registration, renewal, and removal; and
ensure equitable access for communities with limited English proficiency, persons with disabilities, and other underserved groups.

subparagraph.text: The best practices regarding the necessary data elements to be collected and stored, which may include—

clause.text: the address and, where applicable, unit or apartment number;
primary and secondary telephone numbers;
additional contact methods such as email addresses or other secure, verifiable communication channels;
optional verification mechanisms, such as pre-agreed code words or phrases, and contact information for multiple household members; and
associated time frames or conditions (such as expected periods of heightened risk), where applicable, while minimizing the collection and retention of personally identifiable information.

subparagraph.text: The best practices for integrating registry information into call-taking and dispatch workflows, including—

clause.text: automated dispatch flags or alerts when a call originates from, or concerns, a registered address;

guidance for tactical response adjustments when verification suggests a likely hoax, including options for lower-escalation approaches such as staged responses, announcements, or requests for occupants to meet officers outside when safe to do so; and
protocols for documentation and after-action review of incidents involving registered addresses.

subparagraph.text: Recommendations for training call-takers, dispatch personnel, and responding officers on—

clause.text: the nature and risks of swatting;
appropriate use of swatting registry information in assessing risk and selecting tactics; and
avoiding overreliance on unverified registry data while using such data to reduce unnecessary risk.

subparagraph.header: Privacy, civil rights, and civil liberties protections

clause.text: ensure participation is voluntary and based on informed consent;
restrict access to registry data to authorized personnel, with role-based access controls;
require encryption of records at rest and in transit, and other appropriate cybersecurity safeguards;
provide full audit logging of access and use;
prevent misuse of registry information for discriminatory or retaliatory purposes; and
provide notice, redress, and complaint mechanisms for registrants and the public.
reasonable limits on data retention;
procedures for registrants to update or delete their information at any time;
periodic review and renewal mechanisms, including annual prompts or other methods to ensure accuracy; and
appropriate governance, including designation of responsible officers, policy review cycles, and community engagement.
technical approaches for integrating swatting registries with existing 9–1–1 and computer-aided dispatch systems;
secure online portals or mechanisms for registration and updates;
scalability for small and resource-constrained jurisdictions; and
potential Federal resources, including existing grant programs, that may support implementation.

subparagraph.text: Recommended metrics and methodologies to evaluate—

clause.text: impact on safety outcomes for residents, pets, and officers;
impact on property damage, use-of-force incidents, and traumatic forced entries;
impact on litigation exposure and settlement costs; and
impact on operational efficiency and deterrence of swatting.

subparagraph.text: Considerations for how registry information, if appropriately designed and consented to, may safely assist in other types of emergencies (such as medical crises or wellness checks), while maintaining clear limitations and safeguards to prevent overcollection or misuse.

subsection.text: The Attorney General shall make the guidance issued under this subsection publicly available on the website of the Department of Justice, except for any material that would disclose information that is sensitive or classified.

The Attorney General may periodically update the guidance issued under this subsection as appropriate, including to reflect technological developments, emerging threats, and lessons learned from State, Tribal, territorial, and local implementation.
Subject to the availability of appropriations, the Attorney General may provide technical assistance to State, Tribal, territorial, and local public safety agencies seeking to—

paragraph.text: establish voluntary swatting registries consistent with the guidance issued under section 4; or
integrate swatting-related verification and response protocols into existing 9–1–1 and dispatch operations.

subsection.text: The Attorney General shall, to the maximum extent practicable, use existing grant and assistance programs administered by the Department of Justice to disseminate the guidance issued under this Act and to support eligible jurisdictions that choose to design or implement swatting registries consistent with such guidance.

section.text: Nothing in this Act may be construed to—

paragraph.text: authorize the creation or maintenance of a Federal swatting registry;
require any State, Tribal, territorial, or local government to establish a swatting registry; and
limit the discretion of responding law enforcement officers to take actions reasonably necessary to protect life and public safety.

The term swatting means the knowing and intentional making of a false or misleading report to a public safety answering point, law enforcement agency, or emergency service, concerning an alleged ongoing emergency or threat, with the reasonably foreseeable result of prompting an armed or otherwise heightened law enforcement response to a person or address.
The term swatting registry means a voluntary program or database maintained by a State, Tribal, territorial, or local public safety or law enforcement agency that—

subparagraph.text: allows individuals at an elevated risk of swatting to register an address and associated contact information;
stores such information in a secure, access-controlled system available to authorized dispatchers and supervisory personnel; and
is designed to support verification and response protocols when an emergency call is received for a registered address.

paragraph.text: The term public safety answering point has the meaning given that term in section 222(h) of the Communications Act of 1934 (47 U.S.C. 222(h)).
